2026-08-11T12:32:10.3492874Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3493280Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3493616Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3494453Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3494940Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3495738Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3498395Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3500442Z >
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3505126Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3510599Z >
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3525016Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3526653Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3526877Z ### How to Use
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3527127Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3528885Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3530476Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3530681Z ```bash
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3532227Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3533435Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3534628Z ```
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3534837Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3535879Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3536464Z ```bash
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3537760Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3539548Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3541163Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3541920Z ```
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3542889Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3543606Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3545861Z ```bash
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3547122Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3548758Z ```
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3548986Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3549354Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3551259Z ```bash
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3553647Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3555367Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3556118Z ```
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3557033Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3557357Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3567562Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3569882Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3573625Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3573839Z ```bash
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3575161Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3576076Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3577697Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3578282Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3579739Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3582062Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3582906Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3583374Z ```
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3583581Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3584758Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3585680Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3585857Z ```bash
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3587188Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3588598Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3590032Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3590497Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3591111Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3591942Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3592494Z ```
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3592696Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3592900Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3594268Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3596103Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3597104Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3605500Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3606867Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3607963Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3608161Z ### Notes
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3608385Z 
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3609451Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3611591Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3613372Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3615086Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3616792Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3618424Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3619522Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-11T12:32:10.3620628Z </mcp-clis>
